title: He wasn’t hiding from Midian.
paragraphs: He was hiding from the possibility that God might actually use him.

Gideon’s answer in Judges 6:15 is not the voice of rebellion. It is the voice of fear:
“Pardon me, my lord,” Gideon replied, “but how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my family.”
That is the ache of a man who already measured himself and came up empty.

Too small.
Too weak.
Too unknown.
Too broken.
And isn’t that how fear talks to us too?

Fear always builds its sermon around insufficiency.
It points to your background.
Your family.
Your failures.
Your lack.
Your weakness.
Then it whispers, “God can use someone else. Just not you.”

Gideon was not called because he was impressive.
He was called because God was present.

The Lord did not answer Gideon with a résumé boost.
He answered him with a promise:
“I will be with you.” (Judges 6:16)

The calling of God does not rest on the strength of the vessel.
It rests on the power of the One who sends.

Because all of us are Gideon apart from Christ.
Weak in ourselves.
Fearful in secret.
Unable to save ourselves.
But Jesus stepped into our weakness, carried our sin on the cross, rose in victory, and now calls trembling people into new life through His grace.

Your fear may be real.
But it is not final.

Your weakness is not proof that God has abandoned you.
It may be the very place where His glory will be seen most clearly.
So stop bowing to the lie that says your limitation cancels your calling.

If Christ is with you, your “least” is not the end of the story.
It is where grace begins.
